turns.doctor_question: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Well, doc, it’s a whole big mess, to be honest with you. They brought me in here... well, my family did, and some folks from the county. See, it all started at the agricultural fair last weekend. I’ve been going to that fair for, gosh, must be forty years now. Ever since I was a young man helping my father with the herd. Anyway, they asked me to give a little talk about some of the new equipment we’ve been using out on the ranch. Nothing too fancy, just a quick rundown for the younger folks. But then, well, I was up there, and I just felt this... this incredible surge of energy, you know? Like I had to show them, really show them, not just talk about it. 

So, right in the middle of my speech, I climbed up onto the big green tractor they had on display. Brand new model, beautiful machine. And I got up in the cab, and I just started jerking the controls around. I mean, really yanking on the levers and the steering wheel. I was trying to demonstrate this 'new pattern' I’d figured out, this whole new way of operating the machinery that was going to revolutionize how we work the fields. I was pulling the hydraulics, shifting the gears, just going back and forth, back and forth, trying to make them see the pattern. And the crowd... well, they started yelling at me to get down. The fair organizers were shouting, my wife was hollering from the front row, but I just... I couldn't stop. I couldn't make my hands stop moving. Even with all that commotion, all those people screaming my name, I just kept right on jerking those controls until security finally had to come up and pull me out of the cab. So, yeah, that’s... that’s why they dragged me in here today.

symptom_reasoning.S022: The patient describes climbing onto a display tractor during a speech and uncontrollably jerking the controls, demonstrating severely inappropriate and agitated behavior.
symptom_reasoning.S034: The patient explicitly mentions feeling an 'incredible surge of energy' that compelled them to act out their demonstration.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever had a period in your life where you felt deeply depressed for weeks at a time?
turns.patient_response:
Depressed? Well, gosh, no. I can't rightly say that I have. I mean, sure, farming is a tough business, you know? You get a bad season, maybe the rain doesn't come when you need it, or a late frost hits the early blooms, and a man might feel a bit discouraged about the yield. That's just the nature of working with the land. You're at the mercy of the elements. But deeply depressed for weeks at a time? No, no, I’ve never really had the luxury of time for something like that. 

You see, when you’re running a herd and managing a couple hundred acres, the day starts at 4:30 in the morning whether you feel like getting out of bed or not. The cows don't care if you're feeling down, they just know their udders are full and they need milking, and the calves need feeding. So you just pull your boots on and get to it. I've always been a doer, you know? Always moving, always got a task in front of me. Even when my father passed—God rest his soul, that was a tough time for the family—I was right back out on the tractor the very next afternoon because the alfalfa needed cutting before a big storm rolled in. The farm just doesn't stop. 

My wife, she sometimes says I don't sit still enough to actually feel things, but I always tell her, I say, the land doesn't wait on feelings. If a fence is busted, it needs mending right then, or you're chasing strays for three counties. So, sitting around feeling low and heavy for weeks on end... that’s just not in my constitution. I've always had too much drive for that, always got to be working on the next project, checking the irrigation lines, maintaining the combines... there's always something keeping my mind occupied and my hands busy. So no, doc, no long stretches of being depressed for me. Just never happened.

symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient explicitly denies ever experiencing periods of being deeply depressed or feeling low and heavy for weeks at a time.

turns.doctor_question: Before this happened at the fair, have you ever had other times when you felt that same kind of unusually high energy or didn't need to sleep?
turns.patient_response:
Well, doc, that energy... it's a funny thing you ask about that, because, you see, the energy has been with me for quite a spell now. It didn't just start at the fair. Oh no, it’s been building up like a pressure valve on a steam engine. You see, lately... well, for a good while now, my sleep has just been... well, it’s been practically non-existent, to be perfectly honest with you. 

I used to be a man who needed his solid six hours, you know, to be right with the world. But lately? Gosh, I’ll tell you, I just don't need it. I don't feel the pull of the pillow at all. Most nights, I’ll just sit down in my old leather recliner—the one by the woodstove in the den, you know, the one with the worn patch on the right armrest where I always keep my coffee mug—and I might doze off for, oh, maybe two or three hours. Max. And some nights? Some nights I don't sleep a wink. Not a single wink. I just sit there in the dark, listening to the house settle, listening to the wind come off the plains, and my mind is just racing with all the things I need to get done, all the new ideas I have for the herd, all the schematics for the irrigation system. 

And the thing is, doc, the really amazing thing is, I’m up before the sun even thinks about rising. I’m talking 3:00 AM, 3:30 AM, and I am wide awake. I don't feel groggy, I don't feel tired, I don't need three cups of coffee to get my blood pumping. I just spring up out of that chair feeling completely charged, like I’ve been plugged into a socket all night. I’m ready to hit the ground running, ready to work the place like I’ve had a full eight hours of rest. I’ll be out in the barn, fixing the baler, organizing the feed bins, maybe even repainting the stall doors before the hired hands even pull into the driveway. My wife, she comes down at six, and she just stares at me like I’m a ghost, asking when I slept. And I just tell her, 'Martha, there’s too much to do, and I feel fantastic.' So, yes, that high energy... it’s been keeping me going, keeping me moving, day and night, night and day, like nothing ever happened. It's just incredible, really, how little rest a man actually needs when he's got a purpose.

symptom_reasoning.S033: The patient describes feeling 'fantastic' and 'completely charged,' indicating an abnormally elevated mood.
symptom_reasoning.S034: The patient reports having unusually high energy that keeps him moving 'day and night, night and day.'
symptom_reasoning.S036: The patient explicitly states he sleeps only two or three hours or not at all, yet feels completely rested and ready to work.
symptom_reasoning.S038: The patient notes that his mind is 'racing' with things to do and new ideas while sitting in the dark.
symptom_reasoning.S040: The patient describes a significant increase in goal-directed activities, such as fixing the baler, organizing feed bins, and repainting stall doors before dawn.

turns.doctor_question: During this time, have you heard any voices or sounds that other people couldn't hear?
turns.patient_response:
Well, doc, now that you mention sounds... it is a strange thing to try and explain, but yes. Yes, I have. You see, we have this section of land out by the north pasture. It is a beautiful piece of ground, really, been in the family since my granddaddy's time, and we run a whole network of irrigation out there. Mostly surface lines, trying to make sure the water gets exactly where it needs to go, you know how it is. Anyway, I will be out there walking those lines, checking for leaks or clogs, and it usually happens right around dusk. 

There is a certain feeling out there at dusk, when the sun is just dipping behind the ridge and the shadows get all long and stretch across the dirt, and the wind finally dies down for the evening. It gets real quiet out there. And that is when I hear them. Clear as a bell, doc, I hear these voices. And they are not coming from the wind or a neighbor's truck radio carrying over the fields, they are coming right up out of the irrigation lines themselves. Now, I know what water rushing through a pipe sounds like, I have been fixing them my whole life, but this is entirely different. These are actual voices speaking to me from inside the pipes. 

They talk to me about the crops. They tell me exactly what is going on with the land. They will point out specific rows and tell me that a certain row is blessed, that the soil is holy and the yield is going to be magnificent. And then I will walk a few paces down to the next section, maybe check a pressure valve, and the voices will warn me that the next row is poisoned. They tell me the dirt is tainted and the roots are soaking in poison and I need to cut the water to that section immediately. 

And the really peculiar thing about it is that it is not just happening when I have all that buzzing energy I was telling you about. Even on the weeks when I am not all fired up, when that engine inside me slows down and I am just doing my chores at a regular, everyday pace without all that electric feeling... I still hear them. The high energy might settle down, but the voices in the pipes stay. They are out there, dusk after dusk, just echoing up through the aluminum and PVC, telling me what is blessed and what is poisoned. I even brought one of the hired hands out there once, a good kid named Tommy, and I told him to put his ear right down by the main line to listen to them, but he swore he just heard water. But I know what I hear, doc, it is as clear as you and me talking right now, just coming right up out of the north pasture...

symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly confirms hearing clear voices coming from irrigation lines that others, like a hired hand, cannot hear.
symptom_reasoning.S034: The patient references experiencing weeks with 'buzzing energy,' feeling 'all fired up,' and having an 'engine inside me,' indicating periods of abnormally increased energy.

turns.doctor_question: {"intent": "Determine the duration of the auditory hallucinations relative to the mood symptoms to differentiate schizophrenia from schizoaffective disorder.", "question": "How long ago did you first start hearing those voices
turns.patient_response:
How long? Well, now, let me sit and cipher on that for a second, doc, because... well, out on the land, you tend to measure time in seasons and cycles, you know, rather than calendar pages. You measure it by the planting, the harvesting, the calving. But if I really trace it back to the very first time I heard them... the very first time one of those coded warnings came echoing up through the aluminum... I’d have to say it’s been right about 11 months now. 

Yes, 11 months. I remember it specifically because it was late last winter, right when the ground was just barely starting to thaw out enough to get a spade into it. We had this terrible freeze that year, just a bitter, biting cold snap that came howling down from the north and busted a couple of the main line joints out by the tree line. I was out there by myself, wearing my heavy Carhartt coat, my hands just freezing right through my leather work gloves, trying to patch up a crack in the PVC before we needed to start moving water for the early spring prep. And that is exactly when it started. Just this low murmur at first, and then those coded warnings, clear as a bell, telling me about the soil. 

So yes, sir, for about 11 months now. Through the spring planting, through the blistering heat of the summer, right on through the fall harvest... those voices and their warnings have been right there in the pipes. It’s become just a regular part of my evening chores, really. You go out, you check the pressure valves, you listen to the pipes, and you get the rundown on what ground is holy and what’s tainted. Eleven months of it. It’s quite a thing to get used to, let me tell you, but... well, like anything else on a farm, you just adapt to the conditions you're given.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient describes fixed beliefs about receiving coded warnings regarding which ground is 'holy' and which is 'tainted'.
symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly confirms hearing voices and murmurs coming from the pipes for the past 11 months.

turns.doctor_question: Out of those eleven months, how much of that time altogether have you experienced that unusually high energy and lack of need for sleep?
turns.patient_response:
Well, doc, if I really look at the calendar and add it all up... it’s been nearly that whole time. I mean, you think about a year on a farm, right? You got your spring prep, like I mentioned, then you move right into the thick of the summer heat where you're praying for rain and moving water constantly, and then before you know it, you’re into the fall harvest and winterizing the equipment. And through almost all of that... I’ve just been running hot. 

It’s like... well, it’s like a tractor that’s just been left idling in high gear, and someone slapped a heavy brick right down on the gas pedal. I just haven't been able to shut the engine off. So, if we are talking about those eleven months since that big freeze... I’d have to say that those charged, sleepless, nonstop stretches have taken up about ten months of this past year or so. 

Ten months, doc. It sounds unbelievable when I say it out loud like that, I know it does. A man shouldn't be able to just keep going and going like that without his body giving out, but I tell you, I just haven't needed the rest. For ten solid months out of the eleven, I’ve been up before the roosters, fixing fences in the pitch dark, overhauling the combine, pacing the floors when I run out of chores... Martha keeps saying I'm going to drop dead of a heart attack pushing myself like this, but I just feel so plugged in. There was maybe a few weeks in there, just a short little spell somewhere in the middle, where the engine kind of idled down to a normal purr and I actually slept a few nights in a row, but other than that? It's been ten months of just absolute, nonstop, electric energy. Just going and going and going.
